title: Independent AI assurance and operating evidence
question: Which records show that AI assurance methods have been adopted, validated, and maintained for named operating systems?
why_it_matters: Risk frameworks and evaluation methods only become operating assurance when institutions select controls, test named systems, act on findings, monitor production behavior, and disclose outcomes.
current_support: FTFN now has the NIST AI RMF Core, AI Metrology Center, TEVV program, and a completed ARIA 0.1 pilot involving five organizations and seven applications across model testing, red teaming, and field testing.
missing_evidence: measured mission, safety, and reliability outcomes
candidate_records: full AI TEVV draft and final standard
agency system-level evaluation and authorization records
production monitoring, incident, and corrective-action evidence
next_action: Follow ARIA into repeat evaluations and the zero-draft outline into a full draft, final standard, conformity-assessment practice, institutional adoption, named authorization, and production evidence.

named_records: Proposed Zero Draft Outline for an AI TEVV Standard
latest_review.stage_result: The assurance shelf now includes a completed multi-level pilot, method-selection resources, and a standards-development trail. It still lacks institution-level adoption, authorization, repeat testing, production monitoring, incidents, and measured operating outcomes.
latest_review.stop_rule: Do not treat a pilot, resource catalog, framework, or zero-draft outline as certification, institutional adoption, or validated operating performance.

notes: Phase 55Y creates a dedicated assurance gap so AI policy and procurement records are not mistaken for tested and maintained operation.
